research_task.title: Explore: Reconstruct finite-time blowup for 3D forced Euler equations via an iterative scheme. Formulate…

summary: An exact affine-strain Euler family gives triangular one-way exponential amplification of a transverse shear, while a variation-of-constants bound shows that a fixed correction cannot blow up at finite time under integrable accumulated strain and integrable projected forcing.

value_assessment.novelty: Unlike the supplied snapshot-certificate, periodic two-wave closure, and Navier--Stokes enstrophy records, this branch baseline isolates an exact forced-amplitude ODE inside a three-dimensional Euler solution and identifies its finite-time integrability threshold.
value_assessment.evidence: A componentwise Euler derivation, characteristic formula, variation-of-constants estimate, independent hand expansion, and an exact-integer sparse-polynomial special-case certificate support the bounded claim.
value_assessment.falsifier: The result would be overturned by a nonzero residual in the displayed general ansatz, a failure of the characteristic formula, or an example with integrable strain and projected forcing but an unbounded solution of the stated scalar amplitude equation.

claims.statement: For the stated affine-strain and transverse-shear ansatz on three-dimensional Euclidean space, the incompressible unforced Euler equations reduce exactly to a scalar transport-amplification equation whose solution has amplitude factor equal to the exponential of accumulated strain.
claims.evidence_summary: Direct componentwise differentiation proves the general identity, and an exact-integer sparse-polynomial calculation verifies a nontrivial special case independently.
claims.verification_method: Recompute divergence, affine pressure cancellation, all cross terms, and the characteristic solution; then run the exact special-case coefficient check.

claims.statement: A fixed scalar correction satisfying a prime equals strain times a plus projected forcing cannot diverge at a finite endpoint when both strain and projected forcing are integrable in time.
claims.evidence_summary: Variation of constants gives an explicit finite uniform bound depending only on the initial amplitude and the two time-integral norms.
claims.verification_method: Differentiate the variation-of-constants formula and apply the triangle inequality with the accumulated-strain bound.

limitations: The affine background and polarization-independent shear are neither periodic nor finite-energy on the full space.
The correction is localized only in transverse variables, not in all three spatial directions.
The projected-forcing lemma does not establish smoothness of a full Reynolds-stress absorbing force after compact localization.
The fixed-amplitude obstruction does not exclude frequency-driven norm growth or loss of uniform estimates across infinitely many scales.
No finite-time breakdown or Millennium-problem conclusion is claimed.
failed_approaches: Finite-time blowup from a single correction under a bounded smooth strain fails because its exponential factor has finite accumulated exponent.
Allowing an unbounded but integrable strain still does not force amplitude blowup; a nonintegrable example makes the affine background singular already.
next_actions: Compute the full residual of a compactly supported divergence-free localization and test scale-uniform smoothness of any absorbing force.
Track amplitude, frequency, support size, and forcing derivatives separately in an accumulating multi-scale schedule.

proposed_tasks.title: Certify compact-localization residual
proposed_tasks.objective: Localize the exact shear with a compactly supported vector potential and derive every component of the resulting Euler residual under affine strain.
proposed_tasks.rationale: The exact baseline is infinite-energy and does not yet justify the claim that a smooth external force can absorb localization errors.
proposed_tasks.success_criteria: An exact divergence-free localized field, a complete residual formula, and scale-explicit bounds for every spatial and time derivative of the proposed force.
proposed_tasks.useful_failure_criteria: A proved derivative lower bound incompatible with force smoothness for a specified amplification and scale schedule.
proposed_tasks.verification_method: Two independent componentwise derivations plus exact symbolic checks on polynomial-cutoff test profiles.

proposed_tasks.title: Audit infinite-scale ODE schedule
proposed_tasks.objective: Specify an accumulating sequence of correction intervals and test whether derivative-norm growth can coexist with summable strain exposure and smooth forcing projections.
proposed_tasks.rationale: The fixed-amplitude obstruction leaves frequency growth and loss of scale-uniform projection bounds as the main unresolved escape routes.
proposed_tasks.success_criteria: A scale-indexed recurrence with explicit summability inequalities that simultaneously imply norm divergence and finite forcing seminorms.
proposed_tasks.useful_failure_criteria: An explicit incompatible pair of necessary summability inequalities for the chosen schedule.
proposed_tasks.verification_method: Exact recurrence algebra and a reproducible bounded parameter search followed by analytic verification of any candidate inequalities.
